clue.text: He operates still outside the law, by night?

definitions.text: He operates still outside the law, by night?

parts.words: He operates still outside the law, by night?
parts.note: a still here is distilling apparatus, worked illegally under cover of darkness, the way bootleg spirit was made

explanation.surface: Someone keeps up illicit activity after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as the adverb 'yet', but it is the noun: the apparatus for distilling spirits. The moon in the name nods to 'by night'.
explanation.definitionFit: An illicit distiller of whisky was so called because the work was done secretly by moonlight.

clue.text: Is depressed by some trouble about parking sign

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the stirred letters go round the sign
trouble means disturb, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: P is the road sign for parking

explanation.surface: Someone feels low after a row over a parking notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' turns SOME into MOES, and 'about' puts it round P.
explanation.definitionFit: To be gloomy and listless is to sulk in low spirits.

clue.text: Running birds is no way to wealth!

parts.note: nought, written as O
ST is the abbreviation for street
wealth is riches

explanation.surface: Running fast is no route to getting rich.
explanation.definitionFit: These large flightless African birds cannot fly but run at great speed.

clue.text: Rules governing free drinks' issue ?

parts.note: playfully read as the requests made when someone buys a round, treating others to drinks

explanation.surface: Regulations on handing out complimentary drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Standing someone a drink means paying for it, so 'standing' orders are free drinks; really they are the permanent rules of procedure of a body.
explanation.definitionFit: Permanent procedural rules of a parliament or society, as well as regular bank payments.

clue.text: What sermons may do in a high church feature

parts.note: a spire is a tall feature of a church, high in the literal sense

explanation.surface: Sermons inspire people in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High church' suggests the Anglo-Catholic wing; it is just a tall part of the building.
explanation.definitionFit: A good sermon stirs and uplifts its hearers.

clue.text: Old officer's flags

definitions.meaning: an obsolete junior infantry rank, with the possessive

explanation.surface: Banners belonging to a former officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly a junior army officer who carried the colours; also the flags flown by ships.

clue.text: Due to love, got married

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, the letter O
got married means wed

explanation.surface: A debt incurred through romance and a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something due is still to be paid, a sum not yet settled.

clue.text: Origin of revolutionary movement

parts.note: revolutionary is read literally as turning round, the invention that began rotation

explanation.surface: Where a political uprising began.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests political revolution; read it as things revolving.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating disc on an axle is the basic device of turning motion.

clue.text: Five hundred is price demanded for release

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
a charge is a price asked

explanation.surface: A fee of five hundred is set for freeing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a prisoner or patient is to let them go.

clue.text: Officers who show mercy before defeats

parts.note: giving quarter is showing mercy to a beaten enemy
masters means defeats

explanation.surface: Officers who are merciful before they conquer.
explanation.definitionFit: Army or navy supply officers responsible for quarters and stores.

clue.text: A way to answer tribesmen

parts.note: a way is a path

explanation.surface: A route to resolving a question about tribesmen.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pathans are the Pashtun people of Afghanistan and north-west Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathans is the older English name for the Pashtun peoples of the Afghan frontier.

clue.text: Strange on board ship to have head in Dickens

indicators.note: being on board a vessel means sitting inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
strange means queer

explanation.surface: An odd sailor is to be put in charge in a Dickens story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is a headmaster: Wackford Squeers runs the brutal Dotheboys Hall school in Nicholas Nickleby.
explanation.definitionFit: Wackford Squeers is the cruel schoolmaster of Dotheboys Hall in Nicholas Nickleby.

clue.text: Hurl round orchestral part -doing this

indicators.note: round says one word is placed around the other, so it encloses it

parts.note: to hurl is to sling
the wind is a section of the orchestra

explanation.surface: Someone flings a section of the orchestra about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing' is slang for cheating, as in 'I've been done'.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for cheating them, so doing is defrauding.

clue.text: He has a record in the right hand

indicators.note: in places one piece within the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A man holds a disc in his right hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph is a man's name, so it stands for a male pronoun.

clue.text: Pale as a White Leghorn ?

parts.note: the White Leghorn is a breed of domestic chicken, here a female bird

explanation.surface: Something as pale as a white farmyard bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pale as' looks like a simile awaiting completion; 'as' is in fact part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means grey and drained of colour, like ash.

clue.text: Russian port for Michael

definitions.meaning: the White Sea port of Arkhangelsk
the chief of the angels in scripture

explanation.surface: A Russian harbour named for St Michael.
explanation.definitionFit: A northern Russian seaport; and Michael, a chief angel of the heavenly host.

clue.text: A Cockney, but 'e's kind-hearted, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the phrase is spoken, as a Cockney would pronounce it

parts.note: a dropped-aitch version of he is tender, said quickly

explanation.surface: A Londoner from the docks may be rough, but he means well.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys drop their aitches, so 'he's tender' comes out much like the answer. The East End of London is the traditional Cockney heartland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cockney is a native of the East End of London.

clue.text: Copy this bridge !

definitions.meaning: a tournament form of the card game in which the same deals are replayed

explanation.surface: Make a replica of this bridge!
explanation.definitionFit: A copy is an exact replica; and the tournament card game where the same hands are replayed at every table.

clue.text: Purge that may rot social structure

indicators.note: a structure is something built, so these letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A laxative might undermine society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Structure' signals the anagram of ROT and SOCIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: This oil from a bean is a traditional laxative, given to clear the bowels.

clue.text: Where a car rug may give partial cover

definitions.text: Where a car rug may give partial cover

parts.words: Where a car rug may give partial cover
parts.note: a rug for a car passenger lies across the knees, and the phrase splits as location plus place

explanation.surface: Explaining where a travel blanket covers you.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in two parts, it says where a rug goes: across the knees; as one word it is partial coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend over part of something is partial covering.

clue.text: First part may indicate second part of pedigree

definitions.text: First part may indicate second part of pedigree

parts.words: First part may indicate second part of pedigree
parts.note: the wrinkles of the first half of the word reveal the years of its second half

explanation.surface: The opening of a family tree hints at its later part.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word: lines on a face can show age. The whole means pedigree.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry or line of descent, as in a family tree.

clue.text: From parts of Durham, a pleasant tree

indicators.note: parts of the following words, taken together, supply the letters

explanation.surface: A pleasant tree grows somewhere around Durham.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a broadleaved tree, source of syrup in Canada.

clue.text: Put on the line, first class red terrier wants a drink

parts.note: A1 means first class, written AI in crosswords
taken as written

explanation.surface: A first-class red dog is hung out, thirsty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrier wants a drink' gives a second route: an AIREDALE terrier lacking ALE. Laundry put on the line is aired.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing put on the clothes line is hung out so that the air dries it.

clue.text: Hire charges mean tears

explanation.surface: Rental costs make someone cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid to a landlord; also rips or splits in cloth.

clue.text: René is ten, roughly: so is she

indicators.note: roughly means approximately, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a French man's name, taken as written without its accent

explanation.surface: René is about ten years old, and so is a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' signals an anagram of RENE IS TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernestine is a woman's name, so it stands for a female pronoun.

clue.text: A favourite quotation?

parts.note: a bookmaker's quoted odds for a race favourite, not a beloved saying

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a best-loved saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quotation' means betting odds offered; a favourite is often quoted at one to one.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds of one to one, a bet that returns the same as the stake.

clue.text: Officer not appreciating caviare

definitions.meaning: from Hamlet, a play was caviare to the populace at large: delicacies wasted on ordinary people

explanation.surface: A military man has no taste for fish roe.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet says a play pleased not the million: 'twas caviare to the general', meaning the public at large.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-ranking army commander; and the general public, to whom refined things are lost, per Hamlet.

clue.text: Mean to declare historical period

parts.note: to aver is to declare
an age is a period of history

explanation.surface: A plan to announce a period in history.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic the mean and the typical value are the same calculation.

clue.text: Lean over, the edge

definitions.meaning: to tilt to one side, as a ship does
the selvage or border of woven cloth

explanation.surface: Someone leans out over a precipice.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship tilting to one side does this; it is also the selvage border of a piece of cloth.

clue.text: Does deep stress make them go over the limit?

definitions.text: Does deep stress make them go over the limit?

indicators.note: make means form or construct, so the letters are built into something new

explanation.surface: A question whether heavy pressure drives people to break speed limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' signals an anagram of DEEP STRESS; the whole clue also asks whether stress produces fast drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedsters are drivers who habitually exceed the speed limit.
